standard_prerequisites.name: Tor amplitude and its behaviour under pullback
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the definition of tor amplitude in an interval and the lemma stating that it is preserved by pullback along a morphism of ringed sites
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the reduction in part (1), where taking the stalk at a point is a pullback of ringed sites.

standard_prerequisites.name: Exactness can be checked on stalks
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Modules on Sites, the lemma allowing the vanishing of the cohomology of a tensor product to be tested at the points of the site
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the converse in part (2) when the site has enough points.

core_obligations: Part (1) (proof lines 12703-12707): taking the stalk at a point p is the pullback along the morphism of ringed sites (p, O_p) -> (C, O), so the pullback lemma applied to E gives tor amplitude in [a, b] for E_p.

Part (2) (proof lines 12709-12716): if C has enough points, the vanishing of H^i(E tensor^L F) may be checked at stalks, and since H^i(E tensor^L F)_p = H^i(E_p tensor^L F_p) the local tor amplitude bounds imply the global ones.
proof_roadmap: Interpret the stalk as a pullback along a point and apply the pullback lemma for tor amplitude.
For the converse, check the vanishing at stalks using the enough-points hypothesis.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that tor amplitude passes to stalks and, when the site has enough points, can be checked there (statement lines 12689-12700). The proof (proof lines 12702-12716) reads the stalk as a pullback along a morphism of ringed sites for the first part and uses the stalk criterion for exactness, together with the compatibility of tensor products with stalks, for the second. H2: two short arguments.
